corrections.reason: The skill asks kids to match each nation to where it lived and how it lived (food, homes, clothing, roles). The Grade 4 skills on early Indigenous and Inuit societies' locations and daily life teach exactly this, so they are direct, needed prerequisites that are missing. Neither is a prerequisite of the other or of g3-soc-indigenous-communities, so there is no redundancy.

g3-soc-local-government is already a prerequisite of g4-soc-political-regions, which is listed here, so it is redundant. Keeping only the direct, more recent prerequisite follows the rule that a listed prerequisite must not be one another listed prerequisite already depends on.

The skill compares Indigenous and European ways of governing, and the reasons include political systems in the mother country. Kids need the Grade 4 idea of how kings, chiefs, and councils governed to make these comparisons, and this is not covered by the listed prerequisites. g4-soc-governance does not depend on either of the other listed prerequisites, so it is direct.

output.notes: I checked every Grade 5 skill for prerequisite existence, grade order, self-reference, redundancy among listed prerequisites, and title/description clarity. The three corrections above are the only clear problems. g5-soc-explorer-motives lists g3-soc-settlement-factors, which is a weak link because explorer motives do not really depend on what makes a town grow. I left it unchanged because the fur-trade concept overlaps, but it could be reviewed. The titles and descriptions read well aloud, and the prerequisite chains otherwise have no later-grade or self-references.
